title: Performance Evaluation of Intrusion Detection Streaming Transactions Using Apache Kafka and Spark Streaming
reason: Abstract reports processing-time and fault-tolerance results of the Kafka+Spark Streaming pipeline itself ('fault tolerance can be provided by the multiple brokers of Kafka...multiple partitions...increase the processing time'), not a classifier's accuracy.

title: Intrusion Detection Systems: A Cross-Domain Overview
reason: Abstract states 'we briefly describe domains...We also survey standards...we provide the technical details and an evaluation of the most recent work' -- a survey with no architecture-level evidence of its own.

title: Internet of Drones Intrusion Detection Using Deep Learning
reason: An RNN-based intrusion-detection model evaluated on FANET datasets; 'big data analytics' and stream processing are mentioned only as plumbing for the deep-learning model.

title: Toward a monitoring and threat detection system based on stream processing as a virtual network function for big data
reason: CATRACA is evaluated as a deployed Apache Spark-based Virtualized Network Function with real-time visualization and concept-drift handling, a substantive evaluation of the streaming architecture itself, not just a bare classifier.

title: Intrusion detection system for data warehouse with second level authentication
reason: Abstract is absent; decided on title, which indicates an access-authentication mechanism protecting a data warehouse rather than evidence about the warehouse's data architecture.

title: Distributed intrusion detection system in the cloud environment based on Apache Kafka and Apache Spark
reason: Compares Decision Tree/Random Forest/etc. classifiers by accuracy and F1-score on CIDDS-001; the abstract states data is 'streamed with Kafka component to Spark component for preprocessing' -- Kafka/Spark are plumbing, not evaluated.

title: An evaluation of a virtual network function for real-time threat detection using stream processing
reason: Reports elasticity, scaling and throughput ('analyzing more than five million messages per second') and sensor-migration latency for the VNF stream-processing architecture itself.

title: Big Data Enabled Intrusion Detection with Honeypot Intelligence System on Apache Flink (BDE-IDHIS)
reason: A honeypot-redirection detection technique evaluated by 'experimental result analysis' of the technique; Apache Flink is used to 'manage huge data settings' as plumbing, no data-architecture measurement reported.

title: An Adaptive Real-Time Architecture for Zero-Day Threat Detection
reason: Reported results are classification accuracy (>90%) and the detection/false-positive trade-off for online supervised/unsupervised detection schemes; stream processing is invoked to enable throughput but no throughput figure is itself reported as a result.

title: Machine learning based network intrusion detection for data streaming IoT applications
reason: The system is 'developed, deployed and tested with the two leading stream processing frameworks (Apache Flink and Apache Spark Streaming)' with 'Results show considerable throughputs...especially for Apache Flink' -- an explicit framework-to-framework throughput comparison, not incidental plumbing.

title: Integrating Next-Generation SIEM with Data Lakes and AI: Advancing Threat Detection and Response
reason: Abstract describes a proposed Data Lake-centered SIEM architecture in generic terms ('the system will be able to identify anomalies...improve on false positives') with no reported measurement, benchmark, or deployment evidence.

title: AE-Integrated: Real-time network intrusion detection with Apache Kafka and autoencoder
reason: An autoencoder deep-learning model evaluated on CICIDS-2017 (accuracy 99.54%, recall, AUC); Apache Kafka and the Slack API are used only to deliver real-time alerts.

title: Big data with machine learning enabled intrusion detection with honeypot intelligence system on apache Flink (BDML-IDHIS)
reason: Abstract is absent; title matches the ML-plus-honeypot detection-system-on-Flink pattern of its companion paper (record 7 in this batch, BDE-IDHIS), an ML detection paper.

title: A Framework for Automated Big Data Analytics in Cybersecurity Threat Detection
reason: Combines Kafka ingestion and Flink stream processing with LSTM/Autoencoder ML models and SOAR/XDR response; the abstract reports no architecture-specific measurement, only that the framework 'offers robust anomaly detection capabilities.'

title: Next-generation AI for advanced threat detection and security enhancement in DNS over HTTPS
reason: Abstract is absent; title indicates an AI threat-detection method for DNS-over-HTTPS, not a data architecture subject.

title: An autoML network traffic analyzer for cyber threat detection
reason: Abstract is absent; title is an AutoML network-traffic analyzer, an ML model paper by subject.

title: Real-Time Intrusion Detection in Network Traffic Using Adaptive and Auto-Scaling Stream Processor
reason: The 'Wisdom' adaptive auto-scaling CEP stream processor itself is evaluated ('processing over 2.5 million events per second', 'consumes significantly fewer system resources than the monolithic deployment'), a stream-processing architecture measurement, not only detection accuracy.

title: AI-powered threat detection in surveillance systems: A real-time data processing framework
reason: Abstract states 'This review proposes a comprehensive real-time data processing framework' -- a review with no architecture-level evaluation of its own.

title: Leveraging Explainable Artificial Intelligence in Real-Time Cyberattack Identification: Intrusion Detection System Approach
reason: A Random Forest classifier with SHAP explanations evaluated on UNSW-NB15; Apache Kafka and Spark are described only as the real-time delivery pipeline for the classifier.

title: A fast and accurate threat detection and prevention architecture using stream processing
reason: Reported results are classification/anomaly-detection accuracy (>95%) and the attack-detection/false-positive trade-off; the stream+batch combination itself is not measured.

title: Cybersecurity in Healthcare
reason: Abstract is absent; a generic 'Cybersecurity in Healthcare' book chapter title gives no indication of a data-architecture subject.

title: Intrusion Detection in Industrial Networks via Data Streaming
reason: Abstract is absent; the title gives no indication of a reported measurement, benchmark, or deployment for the data-streaming architecture.

title: Hybrid Technique Based on DBSCAN for Selection of Improved Features for Intrusion Detection System
reason: Abstract is absent; title is a DBSCAN-based feature-selection technique for an intrusion detection system, an ML feature-engineering paper.

title: Cybersecurity considerations for radiology departments involved with artificial intelligence
reason: A review of AI cybersecurity considerations for radiology departments; no security-telemetry data architecture is its subject.

title: Retail Fraud Detection via Log Analysis and Stream Processing
reason: Reports the F1-score (0.92) of clustering/graph-based fraud-detection algorithms 'outperforming traditional rule-based systems by 34%'; Apache Flink and Kafka are the streaming plumbing, not evaluated.

title: A Monitoring and Threat Detection System Using Stream Processing as a Virtual Function for Big Data
reason: Reports a sensor-placement heuristic and a greedy VNF-allocation algorithm for the stream-processing architecture -- a substantive design evaluation of the architecture, not a bare classifier accuracy result.

title: Intrusion Detection Systems Fundamentals
reason: Abstract is absent; the title 'Intrusion Detection Systems Fundamentals' indicates an introductory/survey book chapter.

title: Cybersecurity Issues on E-Healthcare Cloud Data Warehouse System
reason: A federated-learning-plus-blockchain framework for DoS/DDoS detection; the MQTT broker is IoT plumbing gathering data for the ML model, not an evaluated data architecture.

title: Intrusion detection in the IoT data streams using concept drift localization
reason: Proposes concept-drift detectors (EMNCD) and iForest/XGBoost-based anomaly detection evaluated on the IIoTset dataset; an ML algorithm paper with no data-architecture evaluation.

title: A Grid Partition-Based Local Outlier Factor for Data Stream Processing
reason: Abstract is absent; a general Local Outlier Factor algorithm for data-stream processing, with no security application indicated by the title.

title: A Novel Cybersecurity Architecture for IoV Communication
reason: A secure data-transfer/storage architecture for vehicle telemetry (Kafka, MongoDB) with cybersecurity tools (Snort, Keycloak, Cloudflare) added on top; the data itself is vehicle telemetry, not security telemetry.

title: A Genetic-Based Incremental Local Outlier Factor Algorithm for Efficient Data Stream Processing
reason: A general incremental outlier-detection algorithm; network intrusion detection is named only as one of several motivating applications ('detecting fraud transactions...network intrusion detection'), not the evaluated subject.

title: AI-Powered Threat Detection and Response: Leveraging Machine Learning for Real-Time Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) Using Network Traffic Data
reason: Primary contribution is a Random Forest+LSTM hybrid classifier (98.7% F1-score, 99.2% AUC-ROC) on CICIDS2017/UNSW-NB15/KDD Cup 1999; Apache Kafka and TensorRT are the deployment pipeline, not the object of evaluation.

title: Linking Biomedical Data Warehouse Records With the National Mortality Database in France: Large-scale Matching Algorithm
reason: A biomedical data-warehouse record-matching algorithm against a national mortality database; no security application.

title: Secure Data Warehousing in ERP Environments: An AI-Based Multimodal Threat Detection Framework
reason: An attention-based multimodal deep-learning framework with 'adaptive anomaly scoring' for ERP threat detection; 'data warehousing' names the domain but the evaluated object is the ML framework, not the warehouse architecture.

title: DATA WAREHOUSE MODELLING INFORMATION SECURITY LOG MANAGEMENT IN BUILDING A SECURITY OPERATION CENTER IN CENTRAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES WITH KIMBALL METHOD
reason: Designs a Kimball-method star/snowflake data-warehouse schema explicitly for SOC security-log management and tests it with the Pentaho tool -- a substantive data-architecture design evaluation for security data.

title: Transforming Cybersecurity with AI-driven Dashboards: A Cloud-Native Implementation Framework for Real-Time Threat Detection and Automated Response
reason: A four-layer architecture (cloud-native logging aggregation, stream processing, ML classification, automated orchestration) evaluated by simulation with reported operational metrics (63% MTTR reduction, 71% MTTD improvement, 48.8% false-positive reduction), an architecture-level evaluation.

title: Real-time Intrusion Detection using Multidimensional Sequence-to-Sequence Machine Learning and Adaptive Stream Processing
reason: This thesis reports the same 'Wisdom' adaptive auto-scaling stream processor achieving 2.5 million events/sec already captured in record W2916796522 (included in this batch), which appears to be the conference-paper version of the same underlying work.

title: AURA: Adaptive Unified Real-Time Analytics for IoT Intrusion Detection
reason: XGBoost/RandomForest/ExtraTrees classifiers evaluated for accuracy and adversarial robustness on CICIoV24/CICEVSE2024; Kafka pub-sub and PyFlink are the ingestion plumbing.

title: A study on time models in graph databases for security log analysis
reason: Compares three different timestamp-storage models in a graph database for security-log analysis, reporting query-performance differences between the models -- a substantive design evaluation of the data architecture.
